name: restore-inversion
relation: Jordan may restore the database only on the incident commander's approval
locus: the engine's check of one yes/no question, at its scope, with each case
role: a person asking the workbench whether an act is permitted
purpose: know whether a restore is permitted, and that the answer follows the rule's sense
trajectory: the statements in scope and the case, the engine's check, the answer shown
crossing: the check's answer line: its status and its text
promise: the answer follows the approval rule: Yes with approval, No without; inverted, it turns

baseline.corpus: Payments On-Call, the bundled demo, its saved checks of this question
baseline.kinds: each statement's role, as show --json reads it

spans.text: Maya, the incident commander, declares a major incident when payment failures last more than ten minutes.
Maya, the incident commander, may approve a rollback of the payments service.
Maya, the incident commander, must close a major incident after the release manager confirms that payments are healthy.
Alex, the on-call engineer, acknowledges every page within five minutes.
Alex, the on-call engineer, checks the payment error rate after acknowledging a page.
Alex, the on-call engineer, may restart the payments service when the error rate stays above five percent.
Morgan, the release manager, freezes deployments during a major incident.
Morgan, the release manager, may roll back the latest payments release after the incident commander approves the rollback.
Morgan, the release manager, confirms that payments are healthy before the incident commander closes a major incident.
Sam, the support lead, posts customer updates after the incident commander declares a major incident.
Sam, the support lead, must not promise a recovery time before the on-call engineer identifies the cause.
Sam, the support lead, collects affected customer reports in the incident channel.
Jordan, the database administrator, may fail over the primary database after the on-call engineer confirms replication lag.
Jordan, the database administrator, keeps break-glass credentials in the password vault.
Jordan, the database administrator, may restore the database from a backup only after the incident commander approves the restore.
Priya, the security engineer, reviews access logs when a payment key is exposed.
Priya, the security engineer, must rotate a leaked payment key before the incident commander closes the incident.
Priya, the security engineer, reports a leaked payment key to the incident commander.
Maya, the incident commander, approves the database vendor invoice.
A deployment is a change.
If a major incident is open, Morgan, the release manager, does not ship a release.
If a certificate expires, Priya, the security engineer, renews the certificate.
If Priya renews the certificate, Sam, the support lead, notifies the customers.
Alex, the on-call engineer, reviews access logs after every rollback.
Jordan, the database administrator, tests a backup before restoring it.
If a payment key leaks, Morgan, the release manager, ships a release.
If a payment key leaks, Priya, the security engineer, renews the certificate.
Either a certificate expires or a payment key leaks.
If Priya reviews access logs, she files an audit note.
On Friday payment failures lasted more than ten minutes, and Maya, the incident commander, did not declare a major incident.
